label: assumption:geometric
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{assumption:geometric}
    Throughout this paper, we impose the following geometric conditions, and the corresponding parameters are regarded as {\it a priori} data.
 \begin{itemize}
    \item The Lipschitz domain $\Omega$ is arcwise connected, with Lipschitz constant $L_\Omega>0$.
    \item The conductivity contrast $k>1$, i.e., the inclusion is more conductive than the surrounding medium.
    \item The inclusions are at distance at least $\delta_0>0$ from the boundary $\partial\Omega$, i.e., $D\subset \Omega_{\delta_0}$ where $\Omega_{\delta_0}:=\left\lbrace {x\in\Omega} \; \middle| \; {{\rm dist}(x,\partial\Omega)>\delta_0} \right\rbrace$.
    \item The interior domain $\Omega_{\delta_0}$ is also arcwise connected.
    \item Each inclusion $D$ is a convex polyhedron with edges of length at least $l_0>0$.
    \item The openings of all vertices are assumed to lie in a fixed range $[\vartheta_m,\vartheta_M]\subset (0,2\pi)$.
    \item The openings of all edges are assumed to lie in a fixed range $[a_m,a_M]\subset (0,\pi)$.
    \item The Dirichlet boundary condition $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ is nontrivial, with $\|f\|_{H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)}>0$.
 \end{itemize}

label: prop:aa2
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This follows from the arguments in Remark 6.3 of \cite{Alessandrini2009}. Using Lemma 6.1 and Theorem 6.2 in that paper, we can extend $w$ to an exterior neighborhood $V$ of $\Sigma$ such that the extension $\widetilde{w}$ satisfies $\|\widetilde{w}\|_{H^1(V)}\leq C\|w\|_{H^{1/2}(\Sigma)}$. Moreover, $\widetilde{w}$ solves $\Delta \widetilde{w}=\widetilde{f}$ in $U\cup V$ with a sufficiently small right-hand side $\widetilde{f}$. Then, interior elliptic regularity yields $\|\widetilde{w}\|_{L^\infty(B(x_0,r_0))}\leq \varepsilon$ for some $x_0\in V$ and $r_0>0$, where $r_0$ depends only on the Lipschitz character of $\Sigma$. Finally, we apply \zcref{prop:p1} to this modified equation to deduce the desired estimate.

label: prop:propa-small
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Using the convexity of $D$ and $D'$, there exist affine hyperplanes $P'$ and $P$ such that $P'$ separates $B({\bf v},h)$ from $D'$, and $P\cap \overline{(D\cup D')}={\bf v}$. Denote by $P'_\pm$ the two half-spaces determined by $P'$, with $D'\subset P'_-$. Similarly, let $P_-$ be the half-space determined by $P$ such that $D\cup D'\subset P_-$, and let $P_+$ be the opposite half-space. Then the region $V=(P_+\cap P'_+ \cap \Omega_{\delta_0})\cup (\Omega\setminus \overline{\Omega_{\delta_0}})$ is connected and satisfies $\Gamma_0\subset \partial V$. Consequently, we can find a rectifiable curve $\gamma_{0,{\bf v}}$ connecting $\bf v$ to a point $x_0\in \Gamma_0$ such that $\gamma_{0,{\bf v}}$ stays at distance at least $r_m:=\frac{1}{3}\min\{h,\delta_0\}$ from $\partial\Omega\cup \partial (D\cup D')\setminus (\Gamma_0 \cup B({\bf v},h))$. We also define the domain $U$ by
        \begin{align*}
            U=B({\bf v},h)\cup \left\lbrace {y\in\Omega} \; \middle| \; {{\rm dist}(y,\gamma_{0, {\bf v}})<r_m} \right\rbrace.
        \end{align*}        
        Then we choose $r<\min\{r_0,r_m\}$ small enough to apply \zcref{prop:aa2} to the harmonic function $u-u'$ in the domain $U$, along a curve obtained by slightly modifying $\gamma_{0,{\bf v}}$. Here the quantity $r_0$ depends only on the Lipschitz character of $\Sigma$, which comes from the proof of \zcref{prop:aa2}. It remains to derive H\"older estimates for $u-u'$ and its gradient on $U$ in terms of the distance to $\partial D$.

        The well-known result of De Giorgi-Nash-Moser (Theorem 8.24 in \cite{Gilbarg-Trudinger}) states that solutions to strongly elliptic equations with bounded coefficients are H\"older continuous at interior points. Consequently, $u-u'\in\mathcal{C}^{\alpha_0}(\Omega_{\delta_0})$ for some $\alpha_0>0$. We also introduce $T_0=\|u-u'\|_{\mathcal{C}^{\alpha_0}(\Omega_{\delta_0})}$.
        
        For the gradient $\nabla (u-u')$, we expect blow-up near the boundary $\Gamma_{D\cup D'}$. To control the blow-up rate, we use the decomposition of $u$ and $u'$ into singular and regular parts as stated in \zcref{th:SingDecom}.
        
        We recall that the regular part $u_{\rm reg}$ has $H^{5/2+\epsilon}$ regularity in $D\cup (\Omega\setminus \overline{D})$. By applying Sobolev embedding $H^{3/2+\epsilon}\hookrightarrow \mathcal{C}^{\epsilon}$ in $2.4^3$, we can deduce that $\nabla u_{\rm reg}$ is H\"older continuous in $U$. 
        
        For the singular parts, it is sufficient to work in local spherical or cylindrical coordinates near vertices or edges. Using the estimates of the singularity exponents $\lambda$ and $\mu$, we deduce that the singularity of $\nabla u_{\bf v}$ is at most of type $\rho^{\lambda_1-1}$ and the singularity of $\nabla u_E$ is at most of type $r^{\mu_1-1}$, as shown in \zcref{lemma:esti-grad-edge}. Consequently, the function $x\mapsto {\rm dist}(x,\partial D)\nabla u(x)$ is $\mathcal{C}^{\alpha_1}$ H\"older continuous in $U$ with $0<\alpha_1\leq \min\{\epsilon,\lambda_1, \mu_1\}$.
        
        The same arguments hold for $u'$. Hence, we can deduce that ${\rm dist}(x,\partial D)\nabla (u-u')(x)$ is H\"older continuous in $U$, and thus we can set $T_1=\|{\rm dist}(\cdot,\partial D)\nabla (u-u')\|_{\mathcal{C}^{\alpha_1}(U)}$. Next, we set $\alpha=\min\{\alpha_0,\alpha_1\}$ and $T=\max\{T_0,T_1\}$ and remark that those parameters depend only on {\it a priori} data. 
        
        The remainder of the proof consists in estimating \eqref{eq:propa-small-holder} as $r\rightarrow0^+$ by using the H\"older continuity of these functions. The argument follows Proposition 3.4, Corollary 3.5, and Proposition 3.7 in \cite{moi5}. The value of $\varepsilon_m$ is given by (3.4) in \cite{moi5}.

title: Remark
body_md: By letting $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$, we can deduce the uniqueness result for the inverse conductivity problem for convex polyhedral inclusions. As a significant improvement over the previous result \cite{Barcelo1994}, the assumption on the boundary data can be relaxed to a generic condition as described here.
